chunks: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from al-Hasan b. Musa al-Khashab from Ali b. al-Nu'man from Abdullah b. Muskan from Zayd al-Shahham. He said: I heard al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon him) say:

Whoever undertakes a matter from the matters of the people and acts justly, opens his door, raises his curtain, and looks into the matters of the people, it is a duty upon Allah the Mighty and Majestic to secure him from fear on the Day of Resurrection and to admit him into Paradise.

key_terms.تولّى أمراً: Undertook governance or responsibility over a public matter
key_terms.روعته: His fear or anxiety, referring to the terror of the Day of Judgment
key_terms.فتح بابه ورفع ستره: Opened his door and raised his curtain -- metaphors for governmental transparency and accessibility

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about just rulers and their reward on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that a ruler who governs justly, maintains accessibility to the people by opening his door and removing barriers, and personally attends to their affairs is guaranteed divine protection on the Day of Judgment and admission to Paradise. This hadith establishes the Islamic ideal of transparent, accessible governance.
